text:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — ACME onboarding asks: they want per-route cost breakdown, an “error lens” for top-5 failing routes, and tracing hooks that tie traces to billing ids. They said this is blocking their pilot GA decision.

Ajay Patel: Ack. Can we get an ask doc? I assume per-route cost = token cost attribution by route + infra overhead?

Maria Chen: Yes. They specifically want: 1) 7d and 30d cost by route, 2) sampling-based trace links to requests, 3) error percent + recent example traces in UI.

Taylor Nguyen: For sampling we can reuse trace-sampler v2, but need a quick mapping from request metadata -> route id. Is that present in dataplane headers?

Samir Gupta: We have route metadata in the request envelope (route_name header). Dataplane currently strips some headers for PII — need to confirm route_name is preserved for private deployments.

Olivia Park: @Samir can you confirm preservation for Private (VPC) customers + Dedicated? ACME will run Dedicated but want to be sure no header redaction breaks correlation.

Samir Gupta: Confirmed for Dedicated — route_name preserved. For Private we have an opt-in redaction flag; product needs to indicate enabling it for onboarding.

Ajay Patel: UX question: do we show raw example traces inline or link out to the trace viewer? ACME wants quick context in dashboard rows.

Taylor Nguyen: Suggest: inline compact trace snippet (span duration, error tag) + link to full trace. Keeps dashboard density and linkability.

Maria Chen: Agree. Also ACME asked for sample rate config per-route (so they can bump sampling on high-error routes). Need product decision on exposing that knob in Console.

Samir Gupta: Backend supports per-route sampling already (experiment flags). Exposing in Console requires a small API surface and validations. Estimated 3 dev days + 1 QA day.

Ajay Patel: Cost breakdown: we already emit token counts per request. We need a mapping to route-level chargeback and a smoothing window. Proposal: token_cost = model_cost_per_token * token_count; infra = datasource of infra allocation by GPU-hrs split proportionally.

Taylor Nguyen: Implementation note: infra allocation is tricky. For Dedicated customers we can use reserved allocation percentages. For Hosted, we'll do per-customer shared pool estimate (approx). Need to call this out in doc as approximation.

Maria Chen: Action: draft an onboarding spec with minimal acceptance criteria for ACME pilot. Must include: A) per-route 7d/30d cost cards, B) error lens top-5 routes, C) trace snippets with link, D) per-route sampling toggle, E) privacy opt-in check for Private.

Olivia Park: I'll draft the spec. Can someone add expected SLAs for telemetry freshness? ACME expects near-real-time (<= 60s) for errors but cost can be eventual (15m).

Samir Gupta: Telemetry freshness: traces and errors can be <30s in Dedicated if we bypass batching; cost aggregation pipeline is 5-15m depending on batch window. We can tune but call it out.

Ajay Patel: UX acceptance: show mockups for dashboard row with mini trace + cost sparkline + error % pill. I can mockup by EOD tomorrow.

Taylor Nguyen: One more constraint: adding trace links increases retention scope for PII compliance. Product must sign off and add to legal checklist.

Maria Chen: Noted. Olivia, include compliance checklist item. Also list roll-forward plan if we miss GA: a) soft-launch without inline traces, b) enable sampling toggle later.

Olivia Park: Working on the spec now. Will post a PR in the repo: docs/onboarding/acme-observability-spec.md.

deploy-bot: Reminder: Please add the feature flag name when you create the PR (format: ff.console.observability.acme).

Maria Chen: Thanks — rough timeline ask from ACME: 3 weeks to pilot. Can we do MVP in 2 sprints?

Samir Gupta: Rough estimate: backend + pipeline changes ~2 weeks, Console UI + QA ~1 week. Two sprints tight but possible if we scope inline traces as progressive enhancement.

Ajay Patel: I'll prioritize the mockups and acceptance criteria in the spec. If engineering approves, we push a canary for the dedicated pool only.

Taylor Nguyen: I'll prototype the compact trace snippet component and link behavior.

Olivia Park: Plan: I’ll open the PR today, include acceptance criteria, compliance flags, telemetry freshness, and rollout plan. Requesting reviews from @Ajay, @Samir, @Taylor.

Maria Chen: Perfect. Follow-up check-in Thu 10am sync. If PR is up before then we can review asynchronously. :thumbsup:

Ajay Patel: +1

Samir Gupta: +1

Taylor Nguyen: +1

Olivia Park: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pulls/4123 — note: draft and includes mocked screenshots.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone — let's try to keep ACME pilot in scope and avoid broad productization until pilot feedback.

Olivia Park: Noted. Will add a pilot-only label in the doc.

Maria Chen: Closing loop: owner = Olivia, eng lead = Samir, UX = Ajay, eng support = Taylor.

Samir Gupta: I'll add the feature flag ticket and infra estimate to the PR.
